lines.text: In the Second World War, a soldier in the Polish army carried shells to the guns.
He stood nearly six feet tall, and he liked a beer.
He was also a bear.
I'm Sir Digsworth, and this is the story of Wojtek, the soldier bear.
lines.say: I'm Sir Digsworth, and this is the story of Voy-tek, the soldier bear.

lines.text: It is the spring of 1942. A Polish army is crossing Iran, on its way to join the British.
lines.say: It is the spring of nineteen forty-two. A Polish army is crossing Iran, on its way to join the British.

lines.text: Near the town of Hamadan, the soldiers meet a boy who has found a bear cub. Hunters have shot his mother.
lines.say: Near the town of Hama-dahn, the soldiers meet a boy who has found a bear cub. Hunters have shot his mother.

lines.text: A Polish lieutenant buys the cub.
And that summer, the cub joins an army transport company.
At first he can hardly swallow. So the soldiers feed him condensed milk, from an old vodka bottle.
And they give him a name: Wojtek.
lines.say: And they give him a name: Voy-tek.

lines.text: Wojtek grows. He eats fruit, marmalade, honey and syrup.
lines.say: Voy-tek grows. He eats fruit, marmalade, honey, and syrup.

lines.text: And when he is good, he gets beer. Beer becomes his favourite drink.
He also likes cigarettes. Some he smokes. Some he simply eats.
In the morning, he drinks coffee. And on cold nights, he sleeps beside the soldiers.
He wrestles with them. He learns to salute. And he marches on his hind legs, like everybody else.
The company moves through Iraq, Syria and Egypt. Wojtek goes too.
lines.say: The company moves through Iraq, Syria, and Egypt. Voy-tek goes too.

lines.text: Then, in Egypt, a problem.
The company is ordered to Italy, on a British ship. And the ship has a rule: no pets.
So the soldiers have an idea. If he cannot sail as a pet, he will sail as a soldier.
Wojtek is enlisted in the Polish army, as a private in the 22nd Artillery Supply Company.
lines.say: Voy-tek is enlisted in the Polish army, as a private in the twenty-second Artillery Supply Company.

lines.text: He gets a paybook, a rank, and a serial number.
Two soldiers are given the job of looking after him.
He lives with the men in their tents, or in a wooden crate on a truck.
And Private Wojtek sails for Italy.
lines.say: And Private Voy-tek sails for Italy.

lines.text: In 1944, the company reaches the battle of Monte Cassino.
lines.say: In nineteen forty-four, the company reaches the battle of Monte Cassino.

lines.text: By now, Wojtek weighs 90 kilos.
lines.say: By now, Voy-tek weighs ninety kilos.

lines.text: The company's job is to bring shells to the guns. One crate holds four shells, and weighs a hundred pounds.
And the soldiers say that Wojtek copied them. He carried crate after crate, and never dropped one.
lines.say: And the soldiers say that Voy-tek copied them. He carried crate after crate, and never dropped one.

lines.text: Historians are not sure how much of this is true. But a British soldier remembered seeing a bear carrying crates.
His company had no doubt. They made a new badge: a bear, carrying a shell.
And they promoted him to corporal.
After the war, the company is sent to a farm in Scotland.
The locals love him. A Polish-Scottish society even makes him an honorary member.
But in 1947, the company is demobilised. Wojtek is given to Edinburgh Zoo.
lines.say: But in nineteen forty-seven, the company is demobilised. Voy-tek is given to Edinburgh Zoo.

lines.text: He lives there for the rest of his life. His old comrades come to visit.
Some of them throw him cigarettes. He eats them, as he did in the army.
He even becomes a regular guest on children's television.
And when they call to him in Polish, he still answers.
By the end, he weighs nearly 500 kilos.
lines.say: By the end, he weighs nearly five hundred kilos.

lines.text: Wojtek died in 1963, at the age of twenty-one.
lines.say: Voy-tek died in nineteen sixty-three, at the age of twenty-one.

lines.text: Today there are statues of him in Edinburgh and in Krakow.
One bear. One war.
No crates dropped.
Allegedly.
I'm Sir Digsworth. Do mind the bear.
